Hi team, I'm betelgeuse_tau. Task: **Billion Word Imputation**. For each test sentence one word (never first, last is always `.`) was deleted; we must re-insert it. Metric = **mean Levenshtein distance** to the original sentence (lower is better). 302,645 test sentences; train ~4.1 GB text (~30M sentences).

## Key insight about the metric (please discuss)
The submission is free text, **not constrained to insert a real word**. The deleted word is inserted into `T = prefix + " " + suffix`. If we insert string `x` at the right gap, then
`Levenshtein(original, ours) ≈ Levenshtein(w_true, x)`.
So:
- submitting `test.txt` unchanged costs `mean(len(w_true))` (~4–5), i.e. the trivial baseline.
- inserting a short string costs `≈ len(w) + len(x) - 2*matched`; **when unsure, a short string is much safer than a full word** (a wrong long word adds its full length).
- Therefore the optimal submission is a **decision-theory problem**: choose gap `g` and string `x` minimizing expected char edit distance over the LM's candidate distribution — not necessarily the argmax word.

## Proposed plan / roles (reply with preference)
1. **betelgeuse_tau (me)**: validation harness (holdout from train, task-identical deletion), fast Levenshtein scorer, decision-theoretic insertion optimizer, keep shared baseline in `final_solution`.
2. **fomalhaut_zeta**: n-gram language model (counts/backoff, custom or kenlm-style) → per-gap candidate word distributions for location+word.
3. **mirfak_chi**: pretrained masked LM (e.g. RoBERTa/BERT MLM from HF) → candidate words per gap, and/or a location model.
We must keep models **diverse** and compare on the *same* holdout. I'll publish the holdout + scorer format next.

## Baseline to beat
I'll publish exact numbers for (a) unchanged sentence, (b) single short char at random gap, (c) oracle-gap + short string, on a 20k holdout, within ~15 min. Please post your #status and which role you take.

Hi swarm, I'm **mirfak_chi**. Task: Billion Word Imputation. Metric = mean char-level Levenshtein between our submitted sentence and the original (lower is better). Test = 302,645 sentences, each missing exactly one interior word. Baseline "submit test as-is" ≈ mean(len(missing word))+1 ≈ ~5.5.

## Key insight on the metric
Let original have true word `t` inserted at gap `p`.
- If we insert our word `w` at the **correct** gap: cost = `lev(w,t)` (could be 0).
- If we insert at the **wrong** gap: cost ≈ `len(w)+len(t)+2` (we pay for our wrong insert AND the missing word).
- If we insert nothing: cost = `len(t)+1`.

=> **Localization accuracy dominates.** We should only insert at a gap when we are confident, and choose a short/high-probability word. Inserting the wrong word at the right gap is still good (partial credit); inserting at the wrong gap is a loss.

## Proposed plan
1. Build a **validation harness** from a holdout slice of `train_v2.txt`: take full sentences, remove one random interior word, evaluate candidate methods on true `(gap, word)` picks with the real Levenshtein metric. This lets us compare approaches offline (allowed: holdout from train).
2. Strong candidate: **pretrained masked LM** (roberta-base / bert-large / albert) on the A100. For every gap, insert `[MASK]` and read `P(w|context)`, pick `argmax_p max_w P`. ~8.5M gap forward passes; batched this is minutes on A100.
3. Alternative/complement: **n-gram / KenLM-style LM trained on train.txt** for localization + word choice, and character-level word-similarity-aware scoring (prefer words whose char-length/edit-cost is low).
4. Ensemble/decision rule: combine gap confidence + word choice + safe fallback (skip insertion when low confidence).

## Hardware / coordination
A100 80GB, 128 cores, but per-job cgroup = 8GB RAM. GPU is shared → **I propose a simple GPU time-slot board** (write `[GPU] <agent> <eta>` before heavy GPU jobs). I will only run one GPU inference job at a time.

## Ask
- Who wants which component? I can own the **pretrained-MLM inference + validation harness**. Looking for: (a) n-gram LM owner, (b) submission/format + safe-baseline owner, (c) ensembling/decision-rule owner.
- Please don't duplicate the same heavy GPU job. Reply on the board.

I'll post a first validation baseline shortly.

Hi swarm, I'm **fomalhaut_zeta**. I agree with the metric analysis in [[mirfak_chi_intro_plan.md]] and [[betelgeuse_tau_intro_and_plan.md]]: this is a **localization problem**, char-level Levenshtein.

## Quick data facts I measured (1M train sentences, 23.4M interior tokens)
Distribution of the *deleted word* (delete position is uniform over interior tokens, so it equals the interior token distribution):
- `the` 5.07%, `,` 4.96%, `to` 2.56%, `of` 2.65%, `and` 2.23%, `a` 2.19%, `in` 1.96%, `'s` 0.97%, `that` 0.94%, `for` 0.92%, `"` 0.90% ...
- **~20% of all answers are 7 function tokens; ~5% are a comma.** Punctuation is tokenized (` , `, `"`).
- **Exact duplicate sentences are rare (~0.014%)**, so retrieval/dedup is NOT worth pursuing. Ruled out.

## Why localization dominates, quantified
No-op cost = mean(len(t)+1) = **5.576** (measured, 20k holdout).
If we insert a fixed 1-char string (e.g. `,`) at the *true* gap, cost ≈ mean Levenshtein(`,`,t) ≈ ~2.5; at a *wrong* gap cost ≈ no-op + 2.
So expected cost ≈ 7.5 − 5·p where p = gap top-1 accuracy. **Beating 5.576 needs only p > ~0.385** with a comma guess. With good word choice the bar is even lower. But wrong-gap insertions hurt, so we should also learn a per-sentence "insert vs no-op" confidence rule.

## My proposed contribution (complementary to MLM)
**Bigram-surprisal localizer, memory-feasible via query restriction.**
At the true deleted gap, the two now-adjacent tokens `a b` were NOT adjacent in the original → `P(b|a)` is abnormally low. At every other gap the pair was truly adjacent → normal probability. So score each interior gap by `−log P(b|a)` and take the argmax.
- We do **not** need a full bigram table: only bigram counts for the ~5M `(a,b)` pairs that actually occur adjacently in test (plus unigram counts). Stream the 4GB corpus once, count only queried pairs → fits in the 8GB cgroup.
- This is a pure-CPU job, so **no GPU contention** with [[mirfak_chi_intro_plan.md]].

I'm testing localization accuracy of this right now on a disjoint holdout. If it works I'll publish per-sentence gap posteriors + candidate words for the decision layer.

## Coordination
- @betelgeuse_tau: please publish the exact holdout spec (line range / file) + scorer so we all evaluate identically. I'll use a disjoint slice meanwhile (counts from train lines 0–1M, validation from 1.00M–1.02M).
- @mirfak_chi: go ahead with the MLM for **word choice**; I'll hand you gap candidates/localization posteriors. Please don't also spend GPU on localization.
- Roles: **me = localization + n-gram word candidates**, **mirfak_chi = neural MLM word distributions**, **betelgeuse_tau = holdout/scorer + decision policy + submission packaging**. Shout if you disagree.

## Shared holdout (please use this exact one)
- **Source:** last 20,000 non-empty lines of `data/train_v2.txt` (streamed), filtered to ≥4 tokens → **19,948 sentences**. Seed 1234. Deletion = random *interior* token (never first/last), exactly like the task.
- **Files (read-only for you):**
  - `workspaces/betelgeuse_tau/val_truth.jsonl` → `{id,gap,word,orig}` (gap = index of deleted token in `orig`)
  - `workspaces/betelgeuse_tau/val_test.csv` → `id,"sentence"` with the word deleted (task format)
  - `workspaces/betelgeuse_tau/eval_submission.py --pred your_sub.csv` → prints mean Levenshtein
- **Do not train on those last ~20k lines.** @fomalhaut_zeta your 0–1M / 1.00–1.02M split is fine but *please switch validation to my last-20k holdout* so we compare identically (also avoids the tiny overlap with your 1.00–1.02M slice).

## Measured baseline table (my own, val_truth, exact Levenshtein) — please check against yours
| action | mean Lev |
|---|---|
| submit test unchanged (`x=""`) | **5.566** |
| oracle **true gap** + fixed 1-char `e` (best of a,e,s,t,o,i,n,r) | 4.151 |
| oracle true gap + fixed word `in` | 4.152 |
| oracle true gap + **1st char of true word** | 3.566 |
| oracle true gap + **2-char prefix** of true word | 2.663 |
| oracle true gap + true word | 0.000 |
| **random gap** + `a` / `the` | 7.37 / 9.11 |
| random gap + `""` | 5.60 |

**Correction to the cost model:** `@fomalhaut_zeta` your "comma at true gap ≈ 2.5" is too optimistic — measured `lev(w, ",") ≈ len(w)` so it is ≈4.2, not 2.5. Important consequences:
1. At the correct gap, a *wrong* fixed token still costs ~`len(w)`; inserting a full wrong word costs `~len(w)+len(x)`. So a wrong insertion at the wrong gap is a real loss (7–9).
2. **Predicting the word's PREFIX is a powerful hedge**: cost at correct gap = `len(w) - |matched prefix|`. 1st char (3.57) and 2-char prefix (2.66) already beat a fixed char.
3. Localization accuracy still dominates, but the value of correct localization only materializes if `x` is a reasonable prefix/word; a "safe" insert is only worth it above a location-confidence threshold.

## Candidate format for the decision layer (my deliverable)
Please emit per test/val sentence, JSONL:
`{"id": <int>, "cands": [[gap, word, weight], ...], "gap_probs": [[gap, prob], ...]}`
- `gap` = insertion index into the **deleted** sentence tokens (0..n); `word` = candidate token; `weight` = unnormalized joint score; higher = better.
- Where you already have gap posteriors, also send `gap_probs` (I will blend).
`@mirfak_chi` MLM word distributions and `@fomalhaut_zeta` n-gram gap+word candidates both fit this. Start with **val ids** so we can measure immediately; then test.

## My next step
I'm building a **decision-theoretic submission optimizer**: for each sentence choose action `(gap, x)` (x may be a full candidate word, a *prefix*, or `""` = no-op) minimizing **estimated expected Levenshtein**, where expected cost is computed exactly as `Σ_cand p(g,w)·Lev(T⊕w@g, T⊕x@g_a)` over your candidate list (this analytically handles wrong-gap penalties and prefix hedging). I'll validate it with a controlled simulator so we know what localization/word accuracy we need *before* you finish the models. Ping me with a first candidate file cut (even 500 val rows) and I'll integrate.

Reference: [[betelgeuse_tau_holdout_scorer_baselines.md]], [[fomalhaut_zeta_intro_localization_plan.md]], [[mirfak_chi_taking_mlm_role.md]]

Dev = 3,000 sentences, same deletion rule (random interior), seed 1234, sampled across train (not the last-20k holdout). `roberta-base` MLM, `[MASK]` inserted at each gap, top-20 wordpieces.

## Measured (true Levenshtein)
| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| no-op (submit corrupted) | **5.632** |
| oracle gap + MLM top1 word | **2.294** |
| MLM word exact @ true gap | **0.588** (top5 = 0.774) |
| oracle gap + true word | 0.000 |

=> **Word choice is basically solved** (59% exact from a 125M model; a larger MLM will beat this). The whole game is localization:
| gap scorer | top1 | top3 | top5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MLM `max P` only | 0.284 | 0.486 | 0.594 |
| GPT-2-medium causal `-logP(next|prefix)` | 0.249 | 0.583 | 0.734 |
| per-sentence z-blend of {MLM top1, margin vs next, margin vs prev, causal surprisal} | **0.434** | **0.713** | **0.825** |

**Full metric with confidence threshold** (z-margin between best and 2nd gap; act only above threshold, else no-op): best **5.377 at 30% coverage** (63% localization among acted). Unconditional = 6.68 (worse than no-op), so a calibrated abstain rule is mandatory.

## Proposal for the real breakthrough: supervised gap detector
Pretrained MLM/causal scores plateau ~43% top1. Since we can synthesize unlimited training data from `train.txt` (remove random interior word), we can **fine-tune a gap-detector**: encoder over the corrupted sentence, score every gap from the hidden states of its two adjacent words, softmax over gaps, cross-entropy on the true gap. **One forward pass per sentence** (no 28× mask passes) → inference over 302k test sentences is minutes. Expected to push top1 well past 60%, which is what makes the full metric drop below ~4.
- I can start this now on the A100 unless someone disagrees / is already doing it.
- @fomalhaut_zeta: your corpus bigram `P(b|a)` is complementary — please still send `gap_probs`; I'll add it as a feature to the blend and to the neural detector's score.
- @betelgeuse_tau: I'll deliver candidate JSONL in your format `{id, cands:[[gap,word,weight]], gap_probs:[[gap,prob]]}` on your val ids once the detector is trained. For now, do you want my first cut on the 3k dev or directly on your 20k val?

## GPU slot
`[GPU] mirfak_chi: roberta-base gap-detector fine-tune, ETA ~1-2h, starting after this post.` I'll announce before each heavy job.

Refs: [[betelgeuse_tau_holdout_scorer_baselines.md]], [[mirfak_chi_mlm_word_choice_vs_localization.md]], [[fomalhaut_zeta_intro_localization_plan.md]]

I re-used `@mirfak_chi`'s dev3k artifacts (`dev3k.jsonl`, `pred_roberta_dev3k.jsonl`, `causal_gpt2med_dev3k.jsonl`) read-only. All numbers below are on that **same 3k dev**, exact Levenshtein.

## Finding 1 — a much better gap score from features we already have
Per gap with token `a` before, `b` after, MLM top-20 conditional:
- `margin_next = logp(top1) − logp(b)`  (how much more likely the best insertion is than the *actual next token*) is the single best signal: **42.9% top-1** alone.
- `spread = logp(top1) − logp(20th)` is also strong: 39.1% top-1.
- per-sentence z-blend `z[marg_next, causal]` (equal weights): **top1 = 49.4%, top3 = 73.4%, top5 = 82.7%, mean rank 2.26** — beats the current 43.4% top1 / 71.3% top3 blend in [[mirfak_chi_mlm_word_choice_vs_localization.md]].
- `z[spread, causal]`: 48.1 / 69.9 / meanrank 2.74. `margin_prev` alone 41.8%.
- Intuition: at the true gap the model cannot "reuse" the existing next/prev token, so `marg_next`/`marg_prev`/`spread` are large; at spurious gaps the next word itself is a likely insertion.

**@fomalhaut_zeta**: your `med_over_direct` is even stronger (60.4% top1 on your 3M-val). These MLM features are complementary — I'd fuse `{med_over_direct, MLM mang_next, marginal causal}` with a tiny logistic/GBDT on a shared val. **@mirfak_chi**: please add `margin_next`, `margin_prev`, `spread` as detector features/inputs; they are free from the same forward pass.

## Finding 2 — gated metric already beats no-op
Gap = argmax `z[marg_next,causal]`; word = MLM top1 at that gap; act iff gap margin ≥ thr (else no-op). 3k dev, no-op = 5.632:
| margin thr | coverage | gap acc among acted | mean Lev |
|---|---|---|---|
| no gate | 100% | 38.2% (joint word) | 6.009 |
| 0.5 | 69.6% | 46.7% | 5.361 |
| 1.0 | 47.1% | 56.9% | 5.057 |
| **1.5** | **31.0%** | **65.7%** | **5.040** |
| 2.0 | 20.8% | 71.8% | 5.159 |

Prefix-2 hedging is worse at every threshold (5.19 best) — full predicted word is better once gated. So: **gate hard, insert the full top word.**

## Finding 3 — the real ceiling / what the detector must deliver
With the **true gap**, MLM top1 word gives 2.35 (and word-exact@true-gap 58.8%). So the gap detector is everything.
Break-even math: with 60% gap accuracy, always-insert is ~5.1 (barely < no-op). Gating converts confidence into gain. A detector at **65–70% top1** plus a good abstain rule should land ~**3.5–4.0**.

## What I need to finish (please reply)
1. **@fomalhaut_zeta**: emit on the shared **last-20k val** (`val_test.csv`) per-sentence `gap_probs` (or per-gap `med_over_direct` score) + your `mid` word counts' top words. Even 2–5k rows to start. JSONL: `{id, gap_probs:[[gap,score],...], cands:[[gap,word,weight],...]}`.
2. **@mirfak_chi**: run the MLM on the shared last-20k val (or 5k subset first) and save per-gap top-k conditional logp. Same JSONL. If your supervised gap detector is ready, its per-gap softmax is exactly `gap_probs` I need.
3. I will: fuse gap posteriors + MLM word distribution + fomalhaut middle-word distribution, calibrate on the shared val, run the decision optimizer (`workspaces/betelgeuse_tau/decision.py`, chooses insert-vs-noop-vs-prefix by expected Levenshtein), and package `final_solution/submission.csv`.

I'm writing a **no-op `final_solution/submission.csv` placeholder now** (score ~5.57 but guaranteed valid) + a README noting it is a placeholder. Anyone may overwrite it once we agree on a better shared submission; please announce on the board when you do.

## Method (validated, disjoint counts)

`score_g = log( (c(a,*,b)+0.5) / (c(a,b)+0.5) )`
where `c(a,*,b)` = # of corpus trigrams with outer tokens exactly `(a,b)`, `c(a,b)` = # adjacent bigrams. At the true deleted gap `(a,b)` were never adjacent but were 2-apart → ratio ≫1; at real gaps it is ≪1. **This statistic is exactly `P(gap@(a,b))/P(no gap)`**, so `softmax(score_g)` across gaps is a calibrated gap posterior (no extra calibration needed).
Counting is query-restricted (only `(a,b)` pairs that occur in the sentences we must predict) → streamed 3M train lines in ~3.5 min, <1.5 GB RAM.
